clue.text: Desire to hold member quite close?

indicators.note: the desire word is said to hold the member, so it wraps round it

parts.note: a desire is a wish
an arm is a member, a limb of the body

explanation.surface: Someone longs to keep a body part near them, perhaps in an embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: In hide-and-seek style guessing games you are 'warm' when close to the target, so 'warmish' is quite close; the question mark flags that playful sense.
explanation.definitionFit: In guessing games being warm means nearing the hidden thing, so the mildly warm state is fairly near.

clue.text: See 2
Teacher fighting for accommodation in rent review — 27 10

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher

indicators.note: the fighting word is placed in the rearranged rent letters
a review looks the rent over again and changes it, so the four letters are rearranged

parts.note: war is fighting

explanation.surface: A teacher fights for housing while a rent review is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: '27 10' points to the cross-referenced phrase about the buck: a buck is a male rabbit, so a warren is literally where the buck stops, a joke that backs up 'accommodation'.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrow system is the home in which rabbits are housed, a kind of animal lodging.

clue.text: Two grunting bonkers — that's worth a look

indicators.note: bonkers means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

parts.note: two in Roman numerals is II
taken as written

explanation.surface: A couple of grunting lunatics make quite a spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: The two I's of the Roman numeral join GRUNTING before 'bonkers' mixes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fascinating arouses curiosity, so it merits being examined.

clue.text: Underwear on a prophet

parts.note: hose are stockings or tights, worn as underwear

explanation.surface: A holy man of old is wearing only his undergarments.
explanation.walkthrough: Hosea is a minor prophet of the Hebrew Bible, with a book named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: This Old Testament figure is one of the twelve minor prophets.

clue.text: Crossed lines in hospital department after the best tool

indicators.note: after puts the hospital part behind the word for the best

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is the best of it

indicators.note: the crossed lines sit inside the hospital department's letters

parts.note: A and E is accident and emergency, the casualty department of a British hospital
two crossed lines make the letter X

explanation.surface: A telephone fault in casualty follows the finest piece of equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: A and E (accident and emergency) is what Britons call a hospital's casualty or emergency room.
explanation.definitionFit: A pointed digging implement with a blade on one side is a manual tool.

clue.text: One, before entering upcoming depression, was enterprising

indicators.note: the one-before pieces go into the depression word
in a down clue upcoming means rising, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: a dip is a hollow or depression in the ground
taken as one, spelt out
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone, before falling into a slump, showed real initiative.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upcoming' means read upwards, and 'entering' sends the two clue pieces into the reversed hollow just after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To break new ground as a pioneer is to act with initiative and daring.

clue.text: No players available then, but a solitary person?

definitions.meaning: if the ... of a play is ..., there are no actors to call on
someone marooned alone, like a shipwrecked sailor

explanation.surface: A theatre with no actors to hand wonders whether someone is left all alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipwrecked person left alone on an island is a lonely figure; read as two words it means actors absent.

clue.text: Those of similar maturity go and argue about pedantries, primarily

indicators.note: about suggests moving the letters around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: primarily picks the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: People of the same age set off and quarrel, mostly over fine points.
explanation.definitionFit: A band of people born around the same time forms a cohort defined by years.

clue.text: Looker that's sweet?

parts.note: a looker is an attractive person, and also an ... is a sweet

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, an eye (looker) that is a sweet (candy); in fact it means an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names someone pleasant to gaze at but perhaps lacking substance.

clue.text: Cricketer's ending with an item of his as capital

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: an gives the letter A
a bat is one piece of a cricketer's kit

explanation.surface: A batsman finishes up, bat in hand, and becomes a capital fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabat is the capital of Morocco.
explanation.definitionFit: The Moroccan seat of government is a chief city of a nation.

clue.text: See 27
Crook lied and inmate murdered

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or out of order, so the letters are twisted

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A criminal told lies and a prisoner was killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crook' looks like the noun for a criminal, but here it is an adjective meaning crooked; 'and' simply joins the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be removed by killing, as a gangster disposes of a rival, is to be done away with.

clue.text: Black and white monster caught about half way across zebra crossing, knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over says the hidden letters are read backwards
the letters are caught where the two words meet, halfway across the phrase

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A piebald beast is hit while halfway over a pedestrian crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'caught about half way across' in the definition; it is the hidden-word signal, as an orca is fully defined by 'Black and white monster'. 'knocked over' turns ACRO round.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a big predator marked in black and white.

clue.text: Drop in here to see publicist

indicators.note: in places the drop word inside the here word

parts.note: present means here, in attendance
to sag is to drop or droop

explanation.surface: Pop in here to meet the PR person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop in' reads as pay a visit, but 'Drop' is the inserted piece and 'in' the container signal; 'to see' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A person hired to get publicity for a client in the newspapers does this job.

clue.text: Bank part of this 2 1, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: Bank is a station on the London tube system
the answer to 2 and 1 down, a rabbit warren, is a subterranean system of tunnels

explanation.surface: A financial institution asks whether it belongs to a burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: London's tube is a system of lines below ground; a burrow complex is another such system.

clue.text: Same symbol, man underlining it in black

indicators.note: in puts the pair inside the black word

parts.note: dark means black

indicators.note: in a down clue the man sits under it, as a line under a word

parts.note: taken as written
Tom is a man's name, also a male cat

explanation.surface: A man draws a black line beneath something to mark it identical.
explanation.walkthrough: A ditto mark is the pair of inverted commas written under a word to mean 'the same again'.
explanation.definitionFit: The two little strokes repeat what is written above, standing for an identical entry.

clue.text: Writer, for example, is inset, surprisingly

annotationWithheld.why: Writer, for example, is inset, surprisingly (8): SAY + IS needs to go inside an anagram of SET, but 'inset' would have to give both the containment and SET, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Writer, for example, is inset, surprisingly

clue.text: I earn (but dubiously) as a City gent

indicators.note: dubiously means in a questionable way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A financier admits he gets paid, though in shady ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; the answer more broadly means any town dweller. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gent working in the City lives an urban life, a resident of a town.

clue.text: Great floods possibly dispersing — about time!

indicators.note: about tells us to move the letters around

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Huge inundations finally break up, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispersing' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the fodder; 'about' does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Tides at new and full moon run highest, so these could be counted as big floods.

clue.text: Boss hot on composer, unpinned?

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: unpinned means the pin is taken out of the composer's name

parts.note: Chopin was a Polish composer

explanation.surface: A head man, keen on a composer, has lost his brooch?
explanation.definitionFit: The American slang word, from Japanese, means a leader or chief.

clue.text: Good, unpleasantly wet, small bottled port

indicators.note: bottled means held inside, so the small letter is kept within the wet word

parts.note: dank means unpleasantly damp

explanation.surface: A good but horribly damp little bottle of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' plays on the drink with 'bottled', but it is a harbour city: Gdansk on Poland's Baltic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This Polish city on the Baltic is a major harbour and shipbuilding centre.

clue.text: See 6
One in a suit after a short cut, a banker no more

indicators.note: after puts the suit card behind the haircut

parts.note: a bob is a short haircut
a diamond is a card of one of the four suits

explanation.surface: A card follows a quick trim, and a financier retires.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob Diamond was chief executive of Barclays bank until he resigned in 2012 over the Libor scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Barclays boss resigned in 2012, so he is an ex-chief of a bank.

clue.text: Make money as senior master?

parts.note: to do is to make, as in do a meal
the yen is the money of Japan

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster asks whether earning cash befits his senior rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The most respected elder of a field is its leading figure, the grand old man.

clue.text: Lover's front talked about

indicators.note: talked about means the word is said and we write what we hear

parts.note: the bow is the front of a ship

explanation.surface: A suitor's front is the subject of gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lover's' stands for 'Lover is', the 's linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned word for a boyfriend or male admirer.

clue.text: Raw egg I flipped onto granny's back — that being the plan!

indicators.note: flipped turns the three words over, so they read backwards

parts.note: rare means undercooked, raw
a nit is the egg of a louse

indicators.note: back picks the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A raw egg is tipped onto grandma's back as part of the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' reverses RARE NIT I to give ITINERAR; 'onto' adds Y from the end of 'granny's'.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel schedule sets out a route, which is a plan of a journey.

clue.text: One's served time as a political defector, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a former prisoner has done a jail sentence
read as ex-Conservative, someone who has left the Tory party

explanation.surface: A jailbird turns out to be a turncoat politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A released convict is a former inmate; read cryptically, a person who was once a Tory.

clue.text: County requiring supreme woman to get in there — reminder on president's desk?

indicators.note: the county and the woman pieces get into the there word

parts.note: taken as written
Bucks is short for Buckinghamshire, an English county
top means supreme, best
she is a woman

explanation.surface: A shire demands a top woman come in there.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is Buckinghamshire, a county west of London. Harry Truman kept a sign with this motto on his desk in the White House.
explanation.definitionFit: Truman's desk sign declared that final responsibility rested with him, a reminder of duty.
